we identified a gene expression signature in AML CD34+, which is not shared with the paired AML CD34-, and that the transcript levels of three of these genes (ANKRD28, GNA15 and UGP2) are associated with a poor prognosis in AML.

the AML CD3+ transcriptome is different compared with normal BM CD34+ and that the transcript levels of the AML CD4+ specific genes ANKRD28, GNA15 and UGP2 can be used as independent prognostic markers in normal karyotypic AML.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genes that are specifically expressed in the leukemic AML stem cells and which are of clinical relevance.
the identification of AML CD 34+-specific genes that are prognostically relevant in normal karyotypic AML.
the identification of AML CD 34+ gene expression profiles and the validation of three genes that are associated with a poorer outcome in normal karyotypic AML patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression level of ANKRD 28, GNA15 and UGP2 in the leukemic CD34+ fraction is a novel and independent prognostic factor in normal karyotyping AML.
the expression of these three genes in the CD34+ APL cells may serve as an independent prognostic marker in normal karyo-type AML patients.
the expression of ANKRD, GNA15 and UGP2 in AML patients is associated with an unfavorable prognosis, and that this is independent of the known risk factors FLT3, NPM1 and CEBPA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AML CD4+ transcriptome is different from the CD34− AML transcriptome and that the expression of the genes ANKRD28, GNA15 and UGP2 is a novel prognostic marker for normal karyotype, AML.

the leukemic stem cells (LSCs) of normal karyaotype AML can be separated from the bulk of the leukemic cells, and that a subset of these LSC-specific genes can be identified and that the transcript levels of these genes are prognostic markers in normal karyotypic AML.
the CD34+ fraction is a distinct entity in AML and that gene expression profiling in this fraction may identify novel prognostic markers in normal karyotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD34+ leukemic cells are not homogeneous, and that the CD34+ leukemogenic stem cells are a small subset of the CD34+ fraction.
the AML CD 34+-specific transcriptome can be used to predict outcome in normal karyo-type AML.
the CD34+ leukemic stem cell fraction can be used to identify genes that predict prognosis and may be potential therapeutic targets in normal karyotypic AML patients.
